h2: Plumber & Pool Service in Kerobokan & Umalas
intro: Kerobokan and Umalas sit between Seminyak and Canggu as quieter, family-oriented villa areas where long-term residents put real daily strain on plumbing, pools and drainage. Bali Fix provides plumber and pool service across both neighbourhoods — from a burst pipe under a garden path to a pool pump that keeps tripping after months of continuous use.

sections.h3: What Breaks Most Often in These Villas
sections.text: Families living full-time in these villas run water heaters, dishwashers and garden taps around the clock, so pipes and fittings wear faster than in short-stay rentals. Add Bali's high groundwater table — similar to what we see in Canggu — and septic tanks plus floor drains need checking after every heavy rain. Older properties in Kerobokan Kelod or Kaja also carry original PVC that cracks at joints, while newer builds nearby introduce different fitting standards. The result is a mix of slow leaks, recurring blockages and heater faults that show up year-round.

sections.h3: Most Requested Services Around Kerobokan & Umalas
sections.text: The calls we get most from this area cluster around three things: water heaters that lose pressure or trip their safety cut-off, irrigation lines leaking under garden beds, and pool equipment — pumps, filters, chlorinators — failing after months of non-stop operation. Blocked drains and septic issues round out the list, especially in villas with large lawns where surface water has nowhere to go. If your villa manager mentions any of these, sending photos over WhatsApp gets you a clear quote before anyone picks up a wrench.

We work across Kerobokan Kelod, Kerobokan Kaja, Umalas, Banjar Anyar and Batu Belig. The area is a patchwork of older two-storey compounds sitting right next to modern builds, so a single street can have both corroded iron risers and brand-new PPR piping. Whatever the age of your property, the approach is the same: diagnose first, explain what's wrong in plain English, then give you a fair price based on the job — no fixed rate cards, just an honest look at the work involved.

sections.h3: Seasonal Tips for Villa Owners Here
sections.text: From October to March, heavy rain pushes groundwater up through septic fields and can back-pressure floor drains; a quick check of your soakaway and drain lines before the wet season saves headaches later. In the dry months (April–September), constant pool circulation dries out pump seals and filter cartridges faster, while irrigation pumps running daily for gardens build up mineral deposits. A short maintenance visit each season keeps both systems from failing mid-summer or after the next storm.

faq.q: How do I get a quote for plumbing or pool work?
faq.a: Send photos or a short video of the issue on WhatsApp and we'll come back with a price based on what the job actually needs — no obligation.

faq.q: Do you handle both older villa pipes and newer installations?
faq.a: Yes. Kerobokan and Umalas have a mix of original iron and PVC runs alongside modern PPR and copper, so we carry fittings for all of them.

faq.q: Can I set up regular pool cleaning and equipment checks?
faq.a: Absolutely — recurring pool service is one of our most common arrangements here, and frequency can be adjusted to how often your villa is occupied.
